content.text: {"headline":"Approve P2: chat deflection, callback on general and overtime 13:00-15:00 lifts the 10:30-15:15 service level to 82.3% for ₹6,576.","why":"A dengue-driven sick wave has left payments at 33 agents against 39 planned and general at 27 against 33. Call volume and handle times are close to forecast, so this is purely a capacity gap. Doing nothing leaves the disruption window at 67.5%, with an 8.1% abandon rate. P2 moves 20% of simple enquiries to chat on both queues, adds IVR callback on general, and offers overtime to 8 agents per queue at the worst hours (13:00-15:00). That gives 82.3% overall (payments 85.7%, general 77.8%) and cuts abandons to 4.4%. It is the cheapest plan that reaches the 80% target within policy, and the rest of the day improves to 87.6%.","trade_offs":["The no-cost option P1 (break shift plus callback) does not help: 66.7% in the window, slightly worse than no action, with general at 60.0%.","P3 adds overtime across the whole gap for ₹10,080, ₹3,504 more than P2. It reaches 84.0% overall and 3.8% abandons.","P3 is the only plan that gets general above 80% (81.9%). Under P2, general stays just short at 77.8% while payments carries the overall figure.","P2 depends on 16 agents accepting overtime and on customers taking up chat. If either falls short, results will be below the forecast."],"watch":"Watch general queue service level and overtime acceptance from 13:00. If general stays well below 78% or fewer than 8 general agents accept, consider extending general overtime earlier, as in P3. Also watch for any further sick calls."}
